reports.note: Multiple reports of trees down and property damage around the Ramsey Street and Linden intersection. Potential start of a tornado track.

EF-1 tornado confirmed. Touched down in the Stone Ridge neighborhood, with a discontinuous path of tree and structural damage northward into the Neuse Crossing neighborhood. Total path length of 2.5 miles, with a peak width of 150 yards, and a duration of 5 minutes.

NWS survey team confirmed an EF-2 tornado in northeastern Newberry County. The tornado touched down near or just before the intersection of Old Blair Road and Henderson Ferry Road where it snapped branches of multiple pine trees and uprooted or snapped several other pines. The tornado crossed the clearing and followed Old Blair Road, snapping and uprooting various hardwood and softwood trees. A home located off of Old Blair Road had several large pine trees snapped or uprooted around the property. There was a small camper on the property which was flipped. As the tornado continued northeastward towards the Broad River it reached the maximum intensity with peak winds estimated to be 115 mph. Much of the forested area along Old Blair Road was destroyed with numerous snapped pine trees found along and north of the road. The trees also brought down several power poles after falling on the poles or attached lines. The tornado lifted just before reaching the Broad River.
Public reported 4 structures destroyed on property with power outage and power line snapped.

Approximate starting point of confirmed EF-1 tornado. A tornado touched down southwest of Louisburg, NC and moved to the northeast before crossing NC-56 just west of Timberlake Rd before dissipating. Mostly tree damage, with some structural and fencing damage was observed, consistent with an EF-1 tornado. Preliminary total path length of 1.93 miles, with a peak width of 130 yards, and a duration of 5 minutes.
Tornado sighted near Rankin St and Beattys Bridge Rd heading northeast toward Hwy 421 and Point Caswell Rd.

Approximate beginning of tornado path. A brief, but strong, short-track tornado occurred on the northeast side of Candor in between Brutonville Road and I-73. Drone images and video provided by Eagle Springs Fire Chief assisted in determining the start point between Cherry Circle and Hurricane Drive where a significant number of uprooted and snapped trees occurred. The tornado quickly continued to track roughly northeast where significant damage occurred to a community center which had 3 of its exterior walls collapsed and several more softwood trees were snapped; consistent with high-end EF-1 to low-end EF-2 damage. The tornado continued across a small pond and snapped about 10 hardwood/softwood trees and removed a large portion of roof covering from a residence near Etta Drive. From this point, the tornado quickly lifted, not before snapping small branches, before reaching I-73 with no visible damage from drone footage to the northeast.

Storm survey found evidence of an EF-2 tornado with estimated peak winds of 115 to 125 mph. The tornado was estimated to be 150 yards wide and 24.43 miles long. The tornado path was found from Wallace to Potters Hill. It should be noted that the tornado may have briefly lifted up at times, and may have been an inconstant path especially near Beulaville toward Potters Hill. The most consistent, concentrated damage was found from west of Wallace, northeast to just west of Chinquapin. At the peak, radar indicated debris lofted as high as at least 12,000 ft, but potentially as high as 16,000 ft.

Approximate beginning of tornado path. The tornado occurred along a 3.2 mile-long discontinuous path, as it momentarily touched down and lifted several times before finally dissipating at the end of the indicated path. Damage consisted mainly of snapped and uprooted trees, large tree branches broken off, minor shingle and roof damage to several homes or structures, many fences blown over, and several power poles that were snapped and downed. There was also damage to patio furniture and signage at a service station at the intersection of Hwy 36 and Hwy 70 in Clayton. The max wind speed was 85 mph which is an EF-0 on the Enhanced Fujita Scale (EF Scale).

A short lived EF-1 tornado developed just south of Beaver Creek Rd, causing EF-1 damage as it crossed the road and moved northeastward. It eventually crossed a small section of the lake before lifting on the northern shoreline. Total path length: 1.07 miles Peak width: 50 yards Time on ground: 1 minute.

A short lived EF-1 tornado developed near the West Regional Library and traveled northeastward. Several trees were snapped in the library parking lot and in the adjacent neighborhood to the north. No structural damage was apparent during the survey, suggesting the strongest winds remained at treetop level.

The path was just over 9 miles with maximum width estimated to be around 350 yards. There was 1 non life-threatening injury reported.

Multiple trees down in this vicinity of Skibo Road and Morganton Road. Suspected beginning of tornado track based on initial reports.

Emergency management reported a brief tornado touched down in Fort Stockton near the intersection of Ryan and Young Streets. The tornado tracked past the Pecos County Courthouse and lifted in James Rooney Memorial Park. A NWS Survey Team found damage to metal roofs and tree branches consistent with a high-end EF-0 tornado.

A brief, weak dusty tornadic circulation, lasting one minute or less, developed with the dust column extending to a rotating cloud base beneath a supercell thunderstorm updraft. Numerous video and pictures of this event were captured by storm chasers.
Several reports of storm damage including 18 wheeler flipped, cars lifted and dropped, roof damage, power outages and trees down around the Walmart and Sams Club along Skibo Road.

The start of the Linden, NC tornado based on NWS storm survey. Maximum winds of 105 mph (EF-1) occurred along Hungry Creek Drive where several windows were blown out of a residence. The tornado tracked along a nearly continuous path for almost 1.25 miles.

Corrects previous tornado report from 3 NE Fort Stockton. Trained spotter and Pecos County EM reported a tornado NE of Fort Stockton. The tornado pulled metal wall panels from a building and overturned a small shed.
Emergency manager reports one building destroyed and another severely damaged along with several large trees snapped in the Hurricane Drive and Hillview street areas.

An EF1 rated tornado developed south of Walker and traveled north-northeast across Walker Road. The estimated maximum wind speed was 105 mph along its 8 mile path. Maximum width was estimated to be 300 yards.
Numerous mature hardwood and pine trees downed, snapped and twisted on Beaver Creek Road, just south of Pea Ridge Road. Damage was coincident with a radar TDS.
Newberry dispatch reported trees down along Old Blair Road. KCAE confirmed debris signature at this time and location.

The start of the Bonnie Doone tornado path based on NWS storm survey. Maximum winds of 115 mph (EF-2) occurred on a short quarter-mile section between the Walmart and Sams Club along Skibo Road while otherwise producing EF-0 to EF-1 damage along a discontinuous path for nearly 5.5 miles.

tracks.note: East Arcadia Tornado confirmed with a combination of damage and video provided by a resident north of East Arcadia. The tornado was broad and evidence suggested that it made intermittent contact with the ground, remaining mostly elevated along the path.

The tornado occurred at a property along Roseland Rd east of Joe Brown Hwy South. Several open farm buildings were destroyed due to roof uplift and subsequent wall failure. Debris was scattered along a narrow path. An empty grain bin was also lifted off its foundation and shifted. Sheet metal roofing was scattered along the path including high into tree canopies and into an adjacent field beyond the grove of trees.

A long-track storm produced mostly EF-0 to EF-1 damage, including a short, quarter-mile stretch of EF-2 damage with maximum wind speeds estimated at 115 mph. The tornado touched down near the intersection of Skibo and Morganton roads, knocking down several trees and removing a couple of HVAC units from the Burlington Shoes store within a strip mall. The tornado then likely lifted briefly before touching down again and intensifying near the Walmart along Skibo Road, where it removed nearly 10 HVAC units from the roof, causing minor damage as they tumbled across it. The tornado continued between two hotels, where it bent and collapsed poles, damaged roofs, and rolled a car or two. As the tornado continued through the Sam’s Club parking lot, roughly a dozen cars were toppled or lifted, and one minor injury was reported. A short-lived tornado with maximum wind speeds of 105 mph initially developed along Ramsey Street near Linden, NC, and continued to track northeast. The most significant damage occurred as the tornado crossed through a residential area between Glenmont Creek Place, Hungry Creek Drive, and Rainy Beck Way. Several homes had minor roof and fence damage; however, a select few along Hungry Creek Drive sustained high-end EF-1 damage, where 50% of the windows were blown out, fence posts set in poured concrete were pulled from the ground, and wind-blown timber punctured exterior walls. The tornado continued tracking northeast into an open area, where drone photos provided by the Harnett County Deputy Fire Marshal revealed a noticeable path through a dormant cornfield and a section of downed or snapped softwood trees in a field north of Horseshoe Bend Road.
